name: miRNA Binding Site Blocking (Target Protector / BlockmiR / miR-Mask)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase expression of a specific target gene by preventing binding of a regulatory miRNA to its binding site on the target mRNA.
molecularDefect: Reduced protein expression caused by pathogenic or excessive miRNA-mediated repression of a disease-relevant transcript.
diseaseMechanism: A disease-associated miRNA binds the 3′ UTR of the target mRNA, suppressing translation and/or promoting mRNA destabilization. Blocking only that interaction restores expression of the specific gene without inhibiting the miRNA globally.
suitableVariantTypes: Haploinsufficiency or reduced protein expression where a pathogenic miRNA:mRNA interaction has been experimentally validated.
typicalDiseases: Frontotemporal dementia (GRN/progranulin deficiency, investigational); additional preclinical cardiovascular, muscular, and neurological disease models.
rnaTargetRegion: miRNA recognition element (MRE), typically within the 3′ untranslated region (3′ UTR) of the target mRNA.
transcriptRequirement: A validated disease-relevant miRNA-binding site within the target transcript.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs including morpholinos, LNA, 2′-O-Me and other fully modified chemistries designed to prevent miRNA binding rather than induce RNA cleavage.
typicalLength: Approximately 15–25 nucleotides depending on the size of the miRNA recognition element and ASO chemistry.
designRules: Literature synthesis: identify experimentally validated miRNA-binding sites; design ASOs complementary to the MRE; avoid RNase H-active chemistries; experimentally confirm restoration of target gene expression.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Target accessible miRNA-binding regions within the 3′ UTR.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential binding to homologous miRNA-binding motifs in other transcripts; evaluate transcriptome-wide complementarity and unintended disruption of other miRNA:mRNA interactions.
advantages: Gene-specific modulation; preserves global miRNA function; fewer systemic effects than anti-miRs because only one miRNA:mRNA interaction is disrupted.
limitations: Requires experimentally validated miRNA-binding sites; limited clinical validation; each target requires a custom-designed ASO.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified. Current therapeutic applications remain preclinical.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic and preclinical evidence; no approved therapeutics.

referencesSummary: Davis et al. (2006); Lima et al. (2018); Staton et al. (2011); Aggarwal et al. (2023).
